title: Buttons
note: Part 10 §F.01. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 guidance compared against ui.rs::button and ui::icon_button; macOS pages read at summary depth only. Found: icon_button has no call site, keyboard focus draws as the hover picture, targets below both platforms' minimums.

title: Text fields
note: Part 11 §F.02. Windows 26H2, GNOME 51 and macOS 27 (summary depth) guidance compared against ui::text_field and the shell's input path. Found: TextEdit (caret, selection, Home/End, Ctrl+A) reaches one Backspace in one dialog; every other field appends at the end; the renderer cannot show a caret index or a selection; a magnifier is drawn in New Folder and Rename fields; no clip, no error/disabled state and no limit tied to the 255-byte name rule.

title: Switches
note: Part 10 §F.03. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 guidance compared against ui.rs::toggle; macOS pages read at summary depth only. Found: a disabled off switch renders identical to an enabled off switch, and Error/Loading/Selected are accepted and ignored.

title: Checkboxes
note: Part 12 §F.04. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 unavailable beyond summaries. Found: the only multi-select checkbox is a hand-drawn 12 px circle (radius = half the side) with an 18 x 18 hit target; no indeterminate or select-all box; Space does not toggle (Enter only); two Tab stops per Files row; no shift-range; no label. The same boolean ("Reduce motion") is a switch in Quick settings and a state-in-label button in Settings and first-run.

title: Radio controls
note: Part 12 §F.05. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 unavailable beyond summaries. Found: no radio control or radio vocabulary exists; the three-way search-engine choice is chips in two different designs (only one has a group label), selected by colour alone despite a comment claiming a check glyph; three Tab stops, no arrow navigation and no selection-follows-focus; theme and language hide their alternatives in cycling rows.

title: Sliders
note: Part 10 §F.06. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 guidance compared against ui.rs::slider; macOS pages read at summary depth only. Found: no surface calls the component (volume is step buttons) and Disabled/Error/Loading/Selected render as Normal.

title: Pickers (date/time/color/file)
note: Part 17 §F.07. Windows 26H2 date/time and colour controls at page depth; the WinUI 3 file-picker page returned 404, so the UWP picker quickstart is cited for the picker information model; Apple pickers and colour wells summary-only; GTK GtkFileDialog read in full; no GNOME HIG picker rule located. Found: the shell has no date, time, colour or file picker (8 picker occurrences, all inline choosers); the clock format is printed read-only, the accent cycles an enum and the wallpaper is enumerated; no control can be unset because no value is ever chosen; no open/save dialog exists.

title: Tabs
note: Part 13 §F.08. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 summary-only. Found: fixed 150 px tabs with no overflow, scroll or cap, so the strip and its + button can leave the window; no tab keyboard model (two Tab stops per tab, no Ctrl+Tab/1-9) while Ctrl+T is Settings' theme cycle; the active tab is a material fill only; close is 15x15 and always visible; the tab menu has Reload and Close only, with no pin/mute/reorder/tear-out. Closing the last tab and clearing stale frames on switch are correct, but closing a tab in front of the focused one handed focus to the tab that took its index (fixed 2026-10-27, BUG-0025).

title: Navigation views
note: Part 17 §F.09. Windows NavigationView read at page depth (five display modes, 52 px header, back button that does not navigate); GNOME view switchers, sidebars and tabs read in full; Apple sidebars summary-only. Found: three navigation idioms (Files places plus breadcrumb, Settings page list, browser tabs and history) with no shared container and no adaptive mode; the Files back/forward/up buttons are always drawn enabled; the breadcrumb has no overflow clamp, no root hotspot and no per-crumb keyboard state; Settings has no back. What is right: one sidebar component with published bounds, and disabled-aware browser history.

title: Sidebars
note: Part 13 §F.10. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 summary-only. Found: two sidebars with two designs (Files 132 px fixed, 20 px rows, fill-only selection; Settings 36 % of the window, 30 px rows, icon and accent marker), no collapse, resize, scroll or compact mode, a Settings sidebar 504 px wide at 1400, no arrow-key model and one Tab stop per row.

title: Command bars/toolbars
note: Part 13 §F.11. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 summary-only. Found: three toolbars with three overflow policies (browser wraps then scales labels, Files silently drops buttons that would collide, Trash uses fixed widths); no overflow menu anywhere; Files draws inapplicable actions as enabled; 22-24 px label-only buttons with no icons, tooltips, access keys or separators; a fixed 112 px confirm button with an 18-character label. The browser's disabled and selected states are real.

title: Menus
note: Part 14 §F.12. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 summary-only. Found: the bar's three labels (Apps, Workspace, Environment) open a launcher overlay, an Activity window and the quick-settings panel -- none opens a menu, and Workspace opening a window contradicts DESIGN-SYSTEM-v3 §3; labels that do not fit are replaced by one chevron whose hotspot opens the launcher, so a dropped label becomes unreachable. The two real menus (LitricOS 2 rows, Power 4 rows, both 34 px rows at 15 px text) have no keyboard binding at all (Key::Menu and F10 are decoded and unbound), no open state on their trigger, no grouping, no disabled or checked row, one Power glyph for sleep, shut down and restart, no ellipsis on the three rows that confirm, and only 1 of their 6 labels exists in the Thai dictionary while the three bar labels never call i18n at all.

title: Context menus
note: Part 14 §F.13. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 summary-only. Found: six surfaces with 28 rows and no keyboard path in (Shift+F10 and the Menu key resolve to nothing) or out (Escape closes overlays only; only a wallpaper click or a chosen row dismisses, and a second right-click re-derives the surface instead); no disabled, checked or radio state, no icons, no shortcuts and no ellipsis on four rows that confirm; destructive rows unseparated and mid-menu; 26 px rows in a fixed 190 px panel with no elision; labels bypass i18n entirely. Files "New folder" from the toolbar or either menu wrote /Documents whatever folder the window showed, because perform_menu read the context_menu that the click had already closed; fixed 2026-10-27 (BUG-0023), as was the second blocker in the same flow -- with the details pane open and no row selected the Files dialog drew no panel and no button (BUG-0024). Right-clicking a Trash row now selects it and a tab menu records the tab it was opened for (BUG-0025); the row test still asserts no panic, not an effect.

title: Tooltips
note: Part 16 §F.14. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 at page depth, macOS at summary depth, measured against 9 glyph-only controls and 3 window buttons. Found: the shell has no tooltip system at all (one comment is the only occurrence), the window buttons reveal their glyph only on hover with no label, hover is the only trigger so a keyboard user cannot learn an icon, and explanations are pushed as notifications instead (32 call sites). Findings F14.01–F14.06.

title: Dialogs
note: Part 15 §F.15. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 read at page depth; macOS 27 from a HIG mirror plus Apple's NSAlert reference. Found: ten dialog presentations (5 Files kinds, 3 desktop kinds, 2 Trash toolbar states) drawn by three implementations with no shared dialog() helper and two button metrics (76x26 against 100x28); a measured probe shows Enter does not accept a Files dialog (it navigates the folder behind it) and that desktop dialogs answer no key at all (Escape and Enter both leave them open); the Files dialog is not modal to the pointer (a click behind the scrim selects a row) and the desktop dialog cancels when its own panel is clicked but not when the desktop is; 23 dialog strings, none through the dictionary though four are already translated; error dialogs print the error type's Display under 'Could not finish'.

title: Sheets
note: macOS sheets: Apple HIG, 8 elements and 4 guidelines, Part 6 §MC.04.06. Windows and Linux sheets were not compared, so this is one platform of three.

title: Notifications/banners/toasts
note: Part 16 §F.17. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 at page depth, macOS at summary depth, measured against the queue model, the banner layer, the centre and the daemon, with a 19-line probe. Found: no action, app icon, group or default action; banners have 0 hotspots and clicking one does nothing; a critical banner never expires and cannot be dismissed where it is; the centre drops the body; the centre answers Escape only; TTL is per call site with no default. Findings F17.01–F17.11.

title: Progress indicators
note: Part 11 §F.18. Windows 26H2, GNOME 51 and macOS 27 (summary depth) guidance compared against ui::progress and its one call site. Found: the Defender scan bar is the only progress in the product (6 px, with a count label); there is no indeterminate/activity form and no spinner anywhere; total==0 renders an empty track during a live scan; ui::badge (a tone-coded status pill) has no call site.

title: Lists
note: Part 10 §F.19. Windows 26H2 and GNOME 51 guidance compared against ui.rs::list_item; macOS pages read at summary depth only. Found: three keyboard models in one shell, 30 px rows in Settings, no accessible names (G.15).

title: Trees
note: Part 17 §F.20. Windows TreeView and GTK GtkTreeExpander read at page depth (chevrons, lazy children, plus/minus and Ctrl+Space); Apple outline views summary-only. Found: no tree control and no hierarchy state anywhere - FileRow carries name, kind, size and mtime only, with no parent, child, depth or expanded flag; the filesystem is a flat table plus drill-in breadcrumbs; the task manager shows PPID and End process tree without drawing a tree; all six list surfaces are flat.

title: Grids/tables
note: Part 18 §F.21. Windows ListView/GridView read at page depth (a table-like collection should use a DataGrid rather than ListView, and WinUI ships none); GTK GtkColumnView read as a reference (sort by header, resize, reorder, TREE_GRID); Apple lists and tables summary-only. Found: two table implementations (Files 22 px header and 24 px rows, three fit-tested columns; Task manager ten columns with width steps and short headers) sharing nothing; the Files draw loop stops at 24 rows and the model has no table-scroll field; no column can be resized or reordered; columns are dropped silently when the window narrows.

title: Cards
note: Part 18 §F.22. GNOME boxed lists read in full (one or two controls per row, background click triggers the control, min and max width, expander rows); no Windows or macOS card rule retrieved. Found: no card component and no ui::card, though the design tokens name cards (litric-design lines 158, 641, 688); Mission Control window cards are ordered stably but share geometry with nothing; the browser start page draws 110 x 48 quick-link tiles with hover only and no focus, pressed or disabled state; neither surface meets the boxed-list contract.

title: Search fields
note: Part 11 §F.23. Windows 26H2, GNOME 51 and macOS 27 (summary depth) guidance compared against the product's five search surfaces. Found: there is no search component; no filter field has a clear affordance; the launcher's ✕ closes the launcher instead of clearing the query; Ctrl+F in Files focuses the table, not the filter; the start-page placeholder names Google regardless of the selected engine; Hot::LauncherSearch is a dead hotspot.

title: Empty states
note: Part 18 §F.24. libadwaita AdwStatusPage read as a reference (icon, title, description and child action slots, compact and spinner variants); no Windows or macOS empty-state page retrieved. Found: at least eight empty states, all text-only (Empty folder, Nothing selected, No pages visited yet, No bookmarks saved yet, Nothing has been downloaded yet, Nothing waiting, the Trash message and the storage Unavailable line); none has an icon, a second sentence or an action; empty, unselected and unavailable are correctly distinguished into three sentences (four for Bluetooth) and the distinction is tested.

title: Loading states
note: Part 18 §F.25. Windows progress controls read at page depth (determinate bar non-blocking, indeterminate bar non-blocking, indeterminate ring blocking, controls read-only, text or nothing for background work); AdwStatusPage spinner paintable as a reference; Apple progress indicators summary-only. Found: State::Loading is well specified and has two product call sites (the Defender scan button and the lock screen unlock); no spinner and no indeterminate form anywhere; one progress bar in the product; no loading state for lists; a slow daemon and a dead daemon produce the same Unavailable sentence.

title: Errors/validation
note: Part 11 §F.26. Windows 26H2, GNOME 51 and macOS 27 (summary depth) guidance compared against fsbridge::valid_name and the two error surfaces. Found: validation runs after submit (and after the daemon on a booted image); a failure replaces the form and loses the typed name; the error detail is elided to one line; the acknowledge button is danger-toned; the Files table's inline error line exists but validation never uses it.

title: Confirmation flows
note: Part 15 §F.27. Same platform reading. Found: 11 confirmation call sites and 7 prompts; 5 of the 7 guard routine work (paste, copy, move, extract, compress) that Windows, GNOME and Apple all say should not prompt because undo is cheaper; permanent delete says 'Delete N selected item(s) permanently?' and the Trash's purge says 'Delete forever?' with no object named; the Trash confirmation is an inline toolbar swap, not a dialog, and takes no focus; no undo exists anywhere (notify carries no action), so reversible actions pay a prompt while irreversible ones have no recovery beyond Trash.

title: Shadows/elevation
note: Part 20: 5 elevation levels, blur 0-44 px, offset 0-20 px, alpha 0-55 percent, monotonic by test. Most shell surfaces are flat, so the scale is defined and tested more than exercised.

title: Materials/blur
note: Part 20: 7 materials and 3 glass presets (blur 32, saturation 115-120, tint 82/85/100 percent); the adaptive solve picks 18-92 percent against the actual wallpaper and high-contrast glass is opaque by design.

title: Icons
note: Part 20: 32 icon variants drawn from one vector module that inherits colour. Icon-only controls still have no label, tooltip or accessible name (Part 16 F.14).

title: Motion timing/easing
note: Part 20: 4 spring tokens with settle budgets 120/200/300/450 ms plus a reduced token; anim.rs assigns them per surface and snaps when reduce motion is set.

title: Light/dark
note: Part 20: 4 themes (Dark, Light, HC Dark, HC Light); Light is separately authored, not an inversion, and the 6-slot accent is refused by high-contrast themes by design.

title: Contrast & high-contrast themes
note: macOS evidence in Part 7; Linux measured in Part 19. 36 of 36 text pairs pass AA (lowest 4.97, Light success), 20 of 20 high-contrast pairs pass AAA (lowest 10.00), but the border token fails 1.4.11 in both standard themes (1.44 Dark, 1.27 Light) while being the only boundary of a field or card. Focus ring is 2 px accent at 90 percent, 6.59:1 Dark and 4.47:1 Light, but State::Focused is unreachable in the button path (Part 10). Windows and GNOME token tables not re-read.

title: Display scaling/HiDPI
note: Part 20: one scale factor in Tokens, set by Shell::set_display(width, height, scale); the layout audit runs every app at two resolutions; no fractional or per-output scale.

title: Multi-monitor
note: Part 20: the compositor registers a single wl_output and the shell keeps one display size and scale; there is no arrangement model, per-monitor DPI or hot-plug path.

title: Localization & RTL
note: Part 20: a 367-line translation dictionary including Thai, and a locale crate feeding hour cycle and first day. Zero RTL or direction handling found in litric-shell or litric-locale.

title: Keyboard-only navigation
note: macOS evidence in Part 7; Linux measured in Part 19 as a route census. The focus ring is consistent and meets a AAA criterion, and the launcher, tabs, Settings search, lock screen and power menu are fully keyboard-operable. But there is no focusable-control model, only rectangle hotspots: menus, context menus, tooltips, the notification centre, breadcrumbs and the non-Files dialogs have no keyboard route, and tab order is per-surface and inconsistent. Windows and macOS keyboard requirement pages not re-read.

title: Screen readers & a11y APIs
note: macOS evidence in Part 7; Linux measured in Part 19. Zero accessibility-API dependencies (no AccessKit, AT-SPI, UI Automation), no accessible name, role, state or relationship store, and no focus or selection events: the shell is drawn pixels on a canvas, so a screen reader has nothing to enumerate. The raw material exists (translation dictionary, non-colour-only states, a genuine AAA high-contrast theme) but the semantic tree does not. Windows and macOS API requirements not retrieved.

title: Pointer/touch/trackpad
note: Part 20: pointer, wheel and keyboard only; no touch event type is handled. Hit targets include 18x18 checkboxes, 20x22 nav buttons and 24-30 px rows, below the 40-44 px platform targets.

title: Reduced motion/transparency
note: Part 20: reduce_motion is honoured end to end (preference, token, animation). There is no reduce-transparency setting; glass adapts its own tint instead.

title: Sound & visual feedback
note: Part 20: no audio output path in the shell; feedback is visual only (tone-coded badges, banners, inline errors, a counted bell), so a critical notification is silent.
